messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT — Anom spike: /v1/embeddings (burst) + auth failures. 18k req/min observed from concentrated IP ranges. Flag: high UA churn, many different bearer tokens per IP. Paging oncall: @mike_oncall

mike_oncall: Oncall — grabbing telemetry. Are these legit customers or a proxy farm?

jordan_engineer: initial look — auth_failure rate up ~6x for same token prefixes, and we see identical payloads across many IPs (same prompt snippets). smells like credential spray + scraper attempting embeddings.

nitya_prod: Confirmed. Top traffic sources show 3 /8s with massive fanout, likely hijacked proxies. Embeddings batch endpoint getting hammered (batch/stream both). Latency spiking to 2.2s p50 -> p95 7s on embed workers.

ryan_waf: I'm rolling a temporary WAF rule to block the offending ASN ranges and high-rate UA patterns. Will do in staged rollout (5% -> 100%) and watch errors.

mike_oncall: Do it. Also prepare short-term mitigations: reduce embeddings per-client concurrency, lower per-token rate, disable large batch endpoint if needed. We need to avoid cascading worker OOMs.

nitya_prod: On it. Reducing per-client concurrent embed requests to 2 and set per-token rate cap to 60rpm. Also disabling /v1/embeddings:batch for public tier.

ops-bot: Executing policy changes:
```
# reduce per-client concurrency
redwoodctl quotas set --route "/v1/embeddings" --concurrency 2
# per-token rate cap
redwoodctl quotas set --route "/v1/embeddings" --rate 60/m --scope token
# disable batch endpoint for public
redwoodctl feature-toggle set embeddings_batch --env prod --value off
```

ops-bot: Done — concurrency/rate caps applied, batch endpoint toggle set to off.

emily_cs: Customer impact check — I pulled usage for last 24h. Small number of enterprise accounts (~5) were using large batch embeddings; those are on Dedicated and not impacted. Public/anonymous batch users will see 429s on batch. I'll draft a short customer notice for public status page.

alice_devex: Posting a short note on status + example workaround: switch to streaming per-item embeddings with lower concurrency; add backoff. I'll paste snippet.

alice_devex: ```curl
POST /v1/embeddings
Authorization: Bearer $KEY
Content-Type: application/json
{ "input": ["text1","text2"], "model": "embed-base" }
# paginate client-side, add jitter/backoff
```

ryan_waf: WAF rule in prod 100% applied. Blocking IP ranges and UA fingerprints. Early signal: edge error rate dropped by 40% in blocked ranges.

jordan_engineer: Observed CPU on embed workers normalized p95 -> 1.6s after caps. Estimated risk reduced. However we still see token churn — some attackers switched to lower-rate hit but more IPs. Need longer tail defenses: geo-slicing and progressive quota backoffs.

mike_oncall: Agreed. Next steps: 1) keep WAF rules and monitor for collateral damage; 2) enable geo-slicing to route suspicious regions to more restrictive quota tier; 3) create rate-slice for anonymous tokens (very aggressive). Also prepare canary rollback path if false positives.

nitya_prod: Implemented geo-slicing policy for the top two offending regions to apply stricter quotas. Also added a temporary fallback model variant (smaller embed) for heavy tenants to reduce cost while we stabilize.

emily_cs: Sent customer notice to status page and emailed affected self-serve customers with mitigation steps and ETA for batch re-enable. Link: https://status.redwood.example/incident/1719991234 (draft).

mike_oncall: Any sign of systemic auth compromise (internal keys)?

jordan_engineer: No internal key leaks detected. The token prefixes are consistent with recycled tokens from other services — looks like credential stuffing using user keys. We'll surface logs to security for token owner IDs for follow-up.

ryan_waf: Also added a temporary challenge page (captcha) for the most aggressive proxy hubs at the CDN edge. That cut malicious request rate by another ~30% in early testing.

mike_oncall: Good. I'll hand off to @sara_sre in the next 10m for overnight watch. Document the steps in the incident ticket and assign to security for token owner notification.

sara_sre: acked — I'll take watch. Please add playbook checklist to the ticket (WAF rule IDs, quota commands, feature-toggle state).

incident-bot: Incident ticket created: INC-2023-1719991234. Assigned: security_team, eng-oncall, cs-ops.

mike_oncall: Postmortem items to capture: how the scraper adapted (IP churn strategy), whether we can automate geo-slice triggers, and customer communication timeline. Also eval if we should have pre-baked small-embeddings fallback for public tier.

emily_cs: I'll track outreach and escalate to AMs for any enterprise anomalies.

sara_sre: I'll keep the WAF rules and rate caps in place for now and review logs at +1h and +4h. If everything stable, we'll plan to re-enable batch endpoint to a reduced tier after 24h with monitoring.

mike_oncall: Thanks all — nice fast coordination. :thumbsup: Closing live mitigation phase, handing to watch/cleanup.

incident-bot: Thread archived in incidents channel. Add further notes to INC-2023-1719991234.
